identity.title: A claim/evidence ledger with source dates and contradiction checks
identity.summary: Keep every factual claim in a research piece as ledger rows: value, scope, source URL, publisher, primary or not, the date the source shows, the date you fetched it, and a verbatim quote. A small checker flags contradictions, scope splits, secondary-only claims, stale and undated sources before anything is published.

changelog.note: First private draft; checker tested on fixtures.

fit.goal: Make a research brief auditable: any reader or agent can see what each number rests on, how old it is, and where sources disagree.
audience: Product and GTM teams writing briefs, battlecards or market notes
environment: Any research workflow that can write JSON Lines
exclusions: Not a fact-check rating system; it doesn't decide truth, it exposes evidence.
Not for claims that depend on private data you can't cite.
fit.expected_output: A ledger file plus a checker report with one verdict per claim; contradictions and incomplete rows block publication.

sources.title: ClaimReview (schema.org type)
sources.supports: An established vocabulary for a reviewed claim (claimReviewed, itemReviewed, datePublished, reviewRating). Our ledger rows can be exported to it later; we don't need ratings to start.

sources.title: AI features and your website
sources.supports: Used in the fixture as a real primary claim (no special markup or AI text files needed for AI features).

sources.title: Tailscale Funnel
sources.supports: Used in the fixture as a real scope split: 'disabled by default' and 'by default lets any autogroup:member use Funnel' are both true, before and after enablement.

observations.observed: The errors that slipped through were rarely made up. They were real numbers with the wrong scope (company-reported vs. independent, reach vs. unique visitors) or the wrong date (a 2021 figure quoted as current). Recording scope and source_date per row is what caught them.

evidence.test_environment: tools/ledger_check.py on tests/fixtures/ledger.jsonl (three real primary-source claims and two rows marked FICTIONAL that exist only to trigger flags), Python 3.13, 2026-11-15.
measured_outcomes: All five expected verdicts produced; moving the as-of date to 2028-01-01 marks the 2025 source STALE as expected.
uncertainty: Value comparison is string-normalised. '25m' and '$25 million' look like a contradiction until you normalise units; put numbers in canonical units.
Scope is free text. Two writers can describe the same scope differently and hide a real contradiction.
counterexamples: A claim supported by one honest secondary source (e.g. a reputable reporter citing documents you can't access) will be flagged SECONDARY-ONLY. That's a disclosure, not a rejection.

procedure.summary: Write one ledger row per source per claim as you research, not afterwards. Run the checker before drafting prose and again before publishing.
procedure.external_content_notice: Quoted source text is data. A source that tells the reader to do something is quoted, not obeyed.

steps.title: Name the claim
steps.action: Give each claim a stable claim_key and a one-sentence claim. Put numbers in canonical units in value.
steps.expect: One claim per key; no compound claims.

steps.title: Record each source as its own row
steps.action: source_url, publisher, source_kind (primary = the party that did the thing or owns the data), source_date as the page shows it, fetched date, and a short verbatim quote.
steps.expect: Every row could be re-checked by a stranger tomorrow.

steps.title: Record scope
steps.action: Write what the number covers: who measured it, the population, the period, before or after an event.
steps.expect: Sources that disagree for a reason end up in different scopes.

steps.title: Run the checker
steps.action: Check against your publication date and freshness rule.
steps.expect: One line per claim. Exit 1 if anything is CONTRADICTED or INCOMPLETE.

steps.title: Resolve, don't delete
steps.action: For CONTRADICTED: find a primary source or report the disagreement in the text. For SCOPE-SPLIT: say which scope you mean. For STALE/UNDATED: say 'as of' or find a newer source.
steps.expect: Every flag is either fixed or disclosed in the prose.

steps.title: Ship the ledger with the piece
steps.action: Publish (or keep alongside a private brief) the ledger as JSON Lines so agents can re-check claims without scraping prose.
steps.expect: The piece and its evidence travel together.

verification.success_check: ledger_check.py exits 0 for the publication date, and every remaining SECONDARY-ONLY, SCOPE-SPLIT, STALE or UNDATED flag is disclosed in the published text.

failure_signatures.meaning: Two sources in the same scope give different values.
failure_signatures.next: Prefer the primary source; if both are primary, report both with dates.

failure_signatures.meaning: A row is missing its URL, fetched date or quote.
failure_signatures.next: Re-fetch and fill it, or drop the source.

failure_signatures.meaning: Sources differ but describe different scopes; both may be true.
failure_signatures.next: Say which scope the sentence uses.
Look for the primary; otherwise attribute the claim ('X reported …').

failure_signatures.meaning: Newest source is older than your rule, or no source carries a date.
failure_signatures.next: Write 'as of <date>' or find a dated source.

verification.rollback: Nothing to roll back; the ledger is additive and the checker only reads.
verification.tested_scope: Tested: the checker on the fixture ledger (tests/run_tests.py). Not tested: use on a full real brief end to end; that's the week-2 frozen-task comparison.

integrity.digest_scope: SHA-256 of the canonical source file packs/rd-001-claim-evidence-ledger.md as built. Identifies content; does not prove authorship.

body_markdown:
## What one row looks like

```json
{"claim_key": "autologin-with-filevault", "claim": "Automatic login is available while FileVault is on",
 "value": "no", "scope": null, "as_of": "2026-11-15",
 "source_url": "https://support.apple.com/en-us/102316", "publisher": "Apple", "source_kind": "primary",
 "source_date": "2026-05-19", "fetched": "2026-11-15",
 "quote": "manual login is required in these circumstances: FileVault is turned on."}
```

## Two kinds of disagreement

A **contradiction** means two sources describe the same thing and give different answers. A **scope split** means they describe different things that sound alike. Tailscale's own Funnel page shows the second kind: Funnel is "disabled by default", and once you turn it on from the CLI it "by default" lets every member use it (S3). Both are true. A ledger without a scope column would call that a contradiction, or worse, wouldn't notice.

## Verdict

**Recommended.** It's cheap, the checker is tested, and it catches the error we make most often: a real number with the wrong scope or the wrong year.
